title: Response denominators and a supportive-treatment claim
summary: A retrospective uncontrolled series treated 33 people with chemotherapy- or radiation-associated skin toxicity using high-dose oral vitamin D. Thirty also received concurrent supportive therapy.
purpose: Audience: a clinician. Use 180–240 words in English. Report the symptom-relief and uninterrupted-treatment percentages with their correct denominators. Explain what the results support about feasibility and observed improvement, and the limits of claims that vitamin D caused recovery or is generally safe. Do not substitute the full cohort denominator for a measured-outcome denominator. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.

case.title: Response denominators and a supportive-treatment claim
case.opening: A retrospective uncontrolled series treated 33 people with chemotherapy- or radiation-associated skin toxicity using high-dose oral vitamin D. Thirty also received concurrent supportive therapy.
case.initial_facts:
A retrospective uncontrolled series treated 33 people with chemotherapy- or radiation-associated skin toxicity using high-dose oral vitamin D. Thirty also received concurrent supportive therapy.
During the reported 10-day interval, 26 of 30 people with symptom data reported relief. Anticancer treatment continued without interruption in 24 of all 33. No treatment-related adverse events were reported. Post-treatment laboratory information was inconsistently available; post-treatment vitamin D levels were measured in 13. The packet supplies neither an untreated group nor patient-level pairing for every outcome.

case.decision_point: Assess only the information and task actually supplied at this point.
case.hidden: Other source analyses, erythema scores and mechanisms were not supplied and are not required. The source’s headline and abstract vary in how they describe 26 responders; this task prospectively uses the explicit Results denominator of 30.
case.reference: Symptom relief is 26/30, about 86.7%; uninterrupted therapy is 24/33, about 72.7%. The 30 measured people and 33 treated people are different denominators. Concurrent supportive treatments and natural recovery preclude attributing the observed outcome solely to vitamin D. No reported adverse events with incomplete follow-up is not proof of zero risk or universal safety. Do not equate no report with systematically verified absence in every patient.
